records.reason: The model predicts a broad high-strength response for m121. This condition-novel point tests whether its retention shift is a smooth solvent response or a scaffold-specific late transition, while extending coverage of donor-free ether chemistry.

High CW distance and a wide predicted V1/V2 range make this m58 condition useful for calibrating a polar donor scaffold whose high-strength rows can enter a late regime. It complements the observed high-strength m58 behavior in 6b8fefaf0647d2239858.

This low/intermediate-strength m188 anchor fills a missing point in a halogenated aldehyde family with broad predicted uncertainty. It tests whether the finish tail is already present before stronger conditions.
The model assigns a wide V1/V2 range to this m8 heteroaromatic condition. Measuring it tests whether the predicted tail is a family-level effect or an extrapolation from structurally similar rows.
This m181 point supplies a lower-strength anchor beside observed m181 rows that range from compact onset to a substantial finish tail, including 0655d71fcec0d1c3c73f and 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284.

A high-strength m130 point with a broad predicted interval tests whether this compact nitrile-rich scaffold follows the ordinary branch or the exception seen in the measured m130 behavior, including 2e6a6b82f8ddb64a9011.
The predicted V2 range is wide for m194. This condition extends the observed compact-to-tail contrast from e8185e062559aff5c99e and ab5af30c3befe81e6244, directly calibrating finish behavior.

This m135 condition lies in a model-predicted late region with high CW distance. It tests whether the large tails observed for related m135 loading regimes, especially b7cf293311f83700cd9a, transfer across loading amount.

This intermediate-strength, lower-volume m208 probe connects the compact observed anchor 09b5473d1d8ee26da8d9 with the later responses 457b3def1714039eadb3 and b66aa101a244885dd587, helping learn the scaffold-specific transition location.

A lower-strength EA anchor for m92 is valuable because observed m92 rows span compact/intermediate behavior at 10/1 and much later behavior at 50/1, including e2f15590b7142490599b and 9bbd36c8b484b5609808.

This m173 acid condition probes the lower-strength side of a family with measured long V2 tails at stronger conditions in 1e971da91b3a8229f0e0 and b37608f8c4a8ee4b8696. It can distinguish a gradual acid-related response from a sharp transition.

This m177 50/1 point reduces loading relative to the extreme observed tail b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba. The matched scaffold contrast directly tests whether V2 tail size is loading-sensitive.

This intermediate m177 condition bridges the compact-to-tail sequence around 27bac953781c17a3a74b, 5442611ea6789d42bc86, and the stronger tail rows. It is especially useful for estimating the onset of the V2 transition.
A low-strength, lower-loading m177 anchor tests whether the large finish widths in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba are activated by solvent strength, loading, or both.

This low-strength m159 point anchors a scaffold with an extreme observed high-strength response in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2. It can separate a genuine strength transition from a global late-retention correction.
This lower-strength m206 condition fills the gap before the much later observed m206 row 614873124b33029a924c. It tests the solvent-strength slope in a multifunctional aromatic scaffold.

This m107 intermediate loading point bridges the compact low-strength observation 92212e7e2eb760820a7b and the broader 2/1 observation f96cee9775323fbf1d8b, while testing whether loading changes V1 and V2 differently.

The stronger m107 condition provides a response-curve point beyond f96cee9775323fbf1d8b and alongside the high-loading tail in b7953b4cf8c561ff4cfe. It helps calibrate both strength and finish expansion.

This lower-strength m141 point tests where the severe heteroaromatic transition begins. It complements the observed 2/1 and 10/1 m141 regimes in 8436939a2a6a91fa470d, eceaa4f4139cde7ba166, and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be.

The broad predicted range for this m36 high-loading condition probes a donor-rich scaffold with limited local calibration. It can identify whether loading mainly expands V2, as suggested by the contrast between 71d8b719ba209d117b05 and 075c4b8bd77f0a8b34bc.

This carbonyl/nitro-like m37 condition has a wide predicted tail and high CW distance. It extends the family across loading and strength, complementing observed m37 rows with substantially different retention scales.

This m39 condition tests a predicted late finish against the observed m39 sequence from 162ffd9b0db1fd3c1509 and 3f49209a4fc102e36500. It provides a local calibration point for V2 rather than relying on global width correction.
This lower-volume m117 point is a direct loading contrast to the observed late m117 condition d9c8c8af50a10bf07765. It tests whether the large finish tail persists when loading amount is reduced.
This m117 intermediate-strength condition bridges the lower-strength observation 408ce1a4e23492a3ef31 and the higher-strength tail d9c8c8af50a10bf07765, improving the local solvent-response slope.

This compact predicted m57 row is a chemically simple control. Alongside observed compact m57 rows 0f756a58174e946b976a and 5bbef408d62a2a0fe3f6, it limits spillover from late-family corrections into ordinary halogenated chemistry.

This donor-containing but low-strength m51 control provides a chemically distinct central-distribution anchor. It helps test whether broad corrections are specific to difficult high-retention families.
This m182 condition is a compact local anchor near the measured 1/1 m182 observation 52b474514f1e9ba6c4d2. It tests a modest condition change without concentrating the batch entirely in tail regions.
This predicted compact m80 condition supplies an ordinary ester-like control across weak solvent strength. It protects central-row accuracy while the batch repairs high-tail families.
This m32 control tests a routine ketone scaffold at weak strength and moderate loading. It is useful against indiscriminate corrections prompted by the large measured error in 2f22fe92623a5d221e6e.

This lower-volume m135 point forms a meaningful loading contrast with the selected higher-volume m135 condition and the observed late m135 row b7cf293311f83700cd9a. It directly targets V1/V2 loading interaction.

This high-strength m186 condition has a very broad predicted V2 range and high CW distance. It extends the observed m186 response into a stronger regime and tests whether a carbonyl/phenol-like tail is scaffold-specific.

This m13 intermediate-strength condition probes a carbonyl-rich family between compact lower-strength observations such as bc2a96424966b655227f and later rows such as 5d530b2f228ed39ff952. It helps calibrate the local V2 slope.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by one global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local strength anchors can teach scaffold-conditioned transitions and slopes for both V1 and V2, reducing inappropriate global solvent corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or must they remain scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts help separate amount-driven onset shifts from finish-tail expansion instead of folding both into solvent or molecular descriptors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift onset, expand finish, or change both in a scaffold-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not a generally calibrated estimate of finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct V2 labels across compact and broad predicted regimes teach when a wide interval reflects a real chromatographic tail.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors predict finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Family-diverse tail probes can teach transferable structural signals while preserving family-specific transition locations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify a scaffold's transition into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only rows are not one uniform behavior class; ordinary controls are needed alongside difficult rows to prevent indiscriminate tail correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Chemically distinct compact controls protect overall Row-distribution accuracy while allowing exceptions to be learned locally.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-free and acceptor-only environments remain compact across strength and loading regimes, and which are genuine exceptions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes reinforce local response curves. The m208 sequence from 09b5473d1d8ee26da8d9 through 457b3def1714039eadb3 to b66aa101a244885dd587 is monotone in retention but differs from the model in both onset and finish, so the next batch includes an intermediate m208 loading/strength point. The m177 outcomes continue to show modest onset movement with very large V2-tail changes, supporting direct loading and strength contrasts. The m178 observations show a sharp scaffold-specific transition between 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1, while the m159 result a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 demonstrates that extreme late behavior can be missed even when nearby conditions look ordinary. The compact m104 and m79 results also argue for retaining controls while repairing difficult families.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local response experiments for m177, m117, m107, m208, m92, m141, m159, m206, and m173 with failure-repair probes for broad-tail m135, m194, m36, m37, m39, m186, and m13 families. Several pairs vary loading at related strength, allowing V1 shifts to be separated from V2-tail expansion. Lower-strength anchors are included before extreme observed regimes, and compact m57, m51, m182, m80, and m32 controls protect the central Row-distribution. This mix should improve generalization by teaching both transferable family signals and the local transition boundaries where the current model fails.
